summary: Frontend-only testing of the new Hand-Holding zoom/pan feature in MockReel. Uploaded /tmp/test.webm, verified default framing shows the full arm/hand/phone with no clipping, verified the new 'Hand size & position' sidebar (data-testid=hand-transform-controls) with all four expected controls (hand-zoom-slider, hand-panx-slider, hand-pany-slider, hand-transform-reset-btn), and validated interactive behaviours: canvas drag updates hand H/V (54%, 15%) in hand mode without touching video crop; mouse wheel zooms hand (1.00x -> 1.75x); reset button restores 1.00x / 0% / 0%; environment background stays put while hand+phone scale; realistic handheld motion animates the canvas over time. Regression: in Floating Phone mode, drag still updates Video crop H/V offset (0%/0% -> 100%/30%) and wheel still changes video Zoom (1.00x -> 2.00x). Export MP4 button remains available in hand mode. No JS/page errors during interaction (only a benign Canvas2D willReadFrequently warning triggered by the test's own getImageData calls, and passive-listener preventDefault notices from Playwright synthetic wheel events).

issues: At default zoom 1.00 there is now sizable empty (blurred bg) space to the left/right of the hand because baseFit was reduced. Framing is correct (nothing clipped, all fingers visible) but users may want a slightly larger default zoom (~1.15) to fill the frame better.

critical_code_review_comments: handView.ts: getImageData is called without willReadFrequently:true on the working canvas; browser logs a warning. Minor perf hint only.

App.tsx onWheel handler calls e.preventDefault() but React attaches wheel as passive by default in some versions -> console shows 'Unable to preventDefault inside passive event listener' when synthesised via Playwright. Consider attaching wheel via useEffect + addEventListener('wheel', ..., {passive:false}) to guarantee the video/hand-zoom interaction cannot scroll the page on real trackpads.

Drag sensitivity in Floating mode is 200x (dx*200) so a small drag already saturates H offset to 100%. Not a regression, but consider lowering to ~100x for finer control (same feedback would apply to hand pan which uses 1x — feels correct).
App.tsx is 1274 lines — approaching the 700-line guideline; splitting the sidebar Sections into subcomponents would improve maintainability.
